uncited: Pixels with values in $[0, \text{eps})$ or $(1-\text{eps}, 1]$ are considered saturated/clipped.

For an input pixel vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^C$, the corresponding row contains $x_c \cdot x_{c'}$ for all $c, c' \in \{0, \dots, C-1\}$, followed by $x_c$ for all $c$, followed by a single bias term $1$.
- Time and memory complexity: Not given in the sources.
Iterative Color Matching is used in computer vision and graphics for color correction and style transfer.
